subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity priorities & SLA path
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Alex D'Souza <alex.dsouza@heliomed.com>, Emily Tran <emily.tran@heliomed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HelioMed — discovery follow-up & prioritization

Thanks again for the call this morning — good conversation and helpful context. I wanted to capture the key pain points and propose a clear next-step sequence so we can lock scope and timeline. TL;DR: HelioMed needs predictable, isolated inference for PHI workloads with low tail latency; next step is a short pilot to validate throughput and SLA targets, then a reserved capacity contract.

Recap of what we heard (priority order):
- Compliance: SOC 2 + HIPAA handling (BAA required) is non-negotiable.
- Isolation: single-tenant/reserved pool or VPC-hosted private plane to prevent noisy neighbor risk.
- Latency: p95 generation target <= 120ms for 1–2k request RPS, with occasional spikes for batch reprocessing.
- Throughput: steady-state 500–1,000 inference QPS on smaller models + nightly bulk runs.
- Cost predictability: committed monthly baseline + burst policy for scheduled runs.

Our recommended approach:
1) 4-week technical pilot (start target weeks of Mar 22) — 2 reserved nodes (right-sized) to validate latency, KV-cache benefits, and quantization results.
2) Post-pilot uplift to reserved pool (config example: 8 reserved GPU-equivalents, single-tenant pool) if results meet SLOs.
3) SLA targets to aim for in commercial draft: 99.95% availability, p95 generation latency <=120ms for interactive routes, defined burst policy (2x baseline for nightly windows).

Open items for HelioMed to confirm:
- Are you comfortable with a VPC-hosted private control plane vs on-prem for the initial pilot?
- Procurement timeline (PO lead time / approvals)?
- KMS/HSM requirements for key management?

Attachments: helio-qual-mat.pdf (overview + preliminary sizing assumptions)

Next steps / owners:
- Marissa: will lead commercial path and collect procurement requirements.
- Ben: will own technical onboarding and pilot ops playbook.
- Logan (me): will coordinate SLA draft and exec alignment.

Can you confirm priority order and availability for a 30-min pilot kickoff the week of Mar 15 or week of Mar 22? Happy to adjust per your procurement window.

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: helio-qual-mat.pdf (1.2 MB)]

From: Alex D'Souza <alex.dsouza@heliomed.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Tran <emily.tran@heliomed.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelioMed — discovery follow-up & prioritization

Appreciate the clear write-up, Logan — this matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Compliance: Yes — SOC 2 Type II and a signed BAA are required before any PHI is processed. On-prem is acceptable but we'd prefer a VPC/private control plane if it can meet our audit controls. Can you confirm Redwood's BAA process and typical lead time?

2) Capacity: Our baseline production is closer to 700 QPS with headroom to 1.5k during peak analysis windows. Nightly batch jobs can be throttled but will need larger burst windows.

3) KMS/HSM: We must use a customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS with key rotation) or an HSM in the private deployment. Please outline how keys are stored and how logs are surfaced for audits.

4) Procurement: Typical approvals are ~6–8 weeks for a new vendor. We'll need an early ballpark cost and a pilot statement of work to attach to the internal request.

If you can send a short SLA + pilot SOW and a ballpark monthly run-rate for the 8-reserved-GPU configuration (and an incremental cost for burst capacity), we can begin procurement intake.

On the kickoff: week of Mar 22 would be best.

Thanks —
Alex D'Souza
CTO, HelioMed Systems

Subject: Technical notes & initial ops proposal (HelioMed pilot)

Alex — quick technical follow-up based on Logan's recap and your clarification. High-level config and rationale below.

Recommended pilot config (to validate latency/throughput):
- Pilot: 2 reserved inference nodes (NVIDIA H100-equivalent) with a single-tenant reserved pool in your VPC.
- Post-pilot target: 8 reserved GPUs (split across 4 inference servers) to meet 700–1.5k QPS in steady-state with burst headroom.

Performance notes:
- Expect p95 < 120ms for our smaller family models with batching tuned to 32 tokens / 8 requests.
- KV cache on the prefix side should reduce redundant token generation by ~20–30% for repeated prompts.
- Quantization to int8/4 can reduce memory footprint and increase throughput; we'll validate quality on your eval set during pilot.

Operational pieces I'll deliver for the pilot:
- Pilot ops playbook (runbook for rolling upgrades, node replacement, incident triage) — 5 business days from kickoff.
- Metrics/tracing hooks (p95, p99 latencies, pod CPU/GPU utilization, token counts).
- BAA / compliance checklist items for engineering review.

I've attached a draft SLA and a short tech annex so procurement has something to attach to the intake. Cost note: ballpark monthly committed cost for 8-reserved-GPU equivalent is included in the SLA draft (see sla-draft-v1.pdf). Final pricing depends on region and exact instance SKU.

Attachments: sla-draft-v1.pdf (technical annex + pricing bands)

If this aligns, Logan / Marissa — I'll prepare the ops playbook after kickoff and a short set of eval prompts for quality checks. Alex — we'll also need a contact for your security team to go through the BAA items.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sla-draft-v1.pdf (0.9 MB)]

Subject: Re: HelioMed — discovery follow-up & prioritization

Thanks, all. This is helpful and actionable. Quick confirmations from our side: 

- We agree to proceed with the 4-week pilot starting week of Mar 22.
- Procurement will initiate the intake this week; PO lead time ~6 weeks but we will fast-track for pilot needs.
- Compliance: we require BAA signed pre-pilot. Please share Redwood's standard BAA and the compliance checklist Ben mentioned.
- KMS: we'll use customer-managed AWS KMS keys; we need details on how Redwood integrates and how audit logs are surfaced to our security team.
- SLA: the draft looks reasonable; we have a couple of minor edits (define maintenance windows and a clearer incident severity ladder). We can send redlines to Marissa.

Marissa — I'll loop procurement on a separate thread, but can you please share the commercial/terms and the SOW so we can attach to the intake?

Logan / Ben — please confirm the pilot kickoff date (Mar 23 preferred) and send the BAA + SOW by EOD Wed so we can attach to procurement.

Appreciate the speed.

—Alex
CTO, HelioMed Systems
